brief: UBS CIO downgrades US equities from Attractive to Neutral (relative preference In line), not on a negative view but because risk-reward is becoming more balanced as market drivers shift from accelerating to decelerating growth: earnings growth and the pace of earnings revisions should slow, AI-related capex growth should ease, and ISM Manufacturing should stop accelerating. UBS raised S&P 500 EPS estimates to $360 for 2026 (+29%) and $415 for 2027 (+15%) on stronger Q3 results, but lowered its June 2027 S&P 500 target to 8,000 from 8,400 and introduced a December 2027 target of 8,200. UBS expects the Fed's hiking cycle to end in early 2027, a catalyst partly supporting new highs, provided inflation improves enough to avoid restrictive policy. The AI trade is shifting from infrastructure buildout to monetization, which UBS says must ramp from today's sub-$200bn revenue run rate toward a couple trillion dollars for ROI confidence. UBS downgrades financials (slower growth, weaker deregulation) and energy (Middle East de-escalation) to Neutral/Unattractive, favoring consumer discretionary, health care, industrials and utilities. Scenarios: Goldilocks (AI, de-escalation, 2.5-3.0% GDP) targets 9,500; AI bust targets 5,500.
